$comment: Advisories the dependency audit gate tolerates. Every entry names one advisory by its GHSA id, the install path(s) the exemption covers, and a reason: a bare 'inherited' is what this file exists to prevent. An entry that stops reporting as high/critical makes the gate fail, so a fixed advisory cannot hide here.

accepted.name: brace-expansion
accepted.reason: Inherited from @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent, not reachable from this package. The peer publishes an npm-shrinkwrap.json, which npm treats as authoritative for consumers and installs without re-resolving, so its pinned 5.0.9 survives every install. npm's own 'fixAvailable: true' is misleading here: overrides cannot pierce a dependency's shrinkwrap (verified for both top-level and path-scoped overrides). Upstream fix is a lockfile bump in the peer: it must resolve brace-expansion to 5.0.11 or newer (5.0.12 clears the moderate GHSA-q2hr-2g5m-vwhr as well), which its own ^5.0.8 range already admits without an API change -- the range permitting 5.0.9 is why the pin still says 5.0.9. Remove this entry once a peer release past 0.99.2 ships that bump; tests/dependency-provenance.test.ts fails once the peer pin clears the advisory range.

accepted.name: brace-expansion
accepted.reason: Same inherited copy as GHSA-qhr7-859c-m2p7: the peer's npm-shrinkwrap.json pins brace-expansion@5.0.9 verbatim and overrides cannot pierce it (verified for both top-level and path-scoped overrides). A peer lockfile bump resolving to 5.0.12 clears all three brace-expansion advisories at once, no API change; tests/dependency-provenance.test.ts guards the pin.

accepted.name: undici
accepted.reason: Accepted runtime exposure, inherited from @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent. Unlike the baselined brace-expansion advisories this copy IS reachable at runtime: the peer's startup (cli/setup -> core/http-dispatcher) installs its bundled undici as the global fetch dispatcher before provider SDKs issue requests, so the pinned undici@8.10.2 serves all fetch traffic inside the host Pi process while this extension runs. This package cannot fix it: the peer publishes an npm-shrinkwrap.json which npm treats as authoritative for consumers and installs without re-resolving -- verified that a top-level "undici": "^8.12.2" override leaves the nested copy at 8.10.2, as overrides cannot pierce a dependency's shrinkwrap. The specific impact of GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c in this dispatcher role is unconfirmed (advisory endpoint did not disclose a concrete consequence chain), so the exposure is accepted pending the upstream fix: a peer release bumping undici to >=8.12.2. Remove this entry once a peer release past 0.99.2 ships that bump.
